Alex: Quick note — noticed repeated tail spikes on seq=32 workloads this morning. Head-of-line blocking when short requests pile behind long stream gens.
Maria: Which metric jumped? queue depth or per-token latency?
Alex: queue_depth p95 up ~3x, GPU utilization steady. Looks like evictions + long-running batches are causing wait amplification.
Suresh: We already have lane-based admission but it's pretty blunt. What's the proposed change?
Alex: Thinking of refactoring queueing into an adaptive topology: a low-latency fast-path (deadline-ordered) for short requests and a throughput-oriented pooled lane for long token traces. Add soft-credits and preemptive flushing for strict deadlines.
Olivia: Concern: changing lanes could hurt KV-cache locality. If a request moves lanes mid-exec we may lose pinned KV entries.
Alex: Agree. Proposal includes a cache-affinity tag on entries so we can prefer keeping cache-hot requests on the same slot. Also an eviction policy that weighs affinity.
Dan: We need observability changes: track lane occupancy, preempt_count, cache_affinity_hits, and per-tenant tail percentiles. Without that we can't tune thresholds.
Prashant: Implementation question — do we introduce separate queue structures (fast_queue, pool_queue) or add routing hints to the existing queue nodes? I prefer hints to avoid duplicating queuing logic.
Alex: I like hints too. Routing hint + deadline + tokens_left should be enough to place into a logical topology while reusing the current ring/buffer.
Maria: How does admission decide? simple rule or ML model?
Alex: Start simple. Pseudocode:
```
if tokens_left <= FAST_THRESHOLD and expected_latency < SLO:
  route = "fast"
elif wait_ms > PREEMPT_MS:
  route = "flush"  # preemptive flush to avoid unbounded wait
else:
  route = "slow"
```
Suresh: Starvation prevention? fast lane could drain slow lane.
Alex: We'll use bandwidth reservations + soft-credits for slow lane and periodic headroom drains for fast lane. Also fallback: if slow-lane wait > X then force a small-pop of slow lane.
Olivia: On cache-affinity: we can add a small per-slot pin budget. Pins evicted by LRU weighted by lane_priority. Need to measure memory pressure.
Dan: I'll add microbenchmarks: pinned-kv eviction cost, lane-switch latency, and tail p99 with mixtures (80/20 short/long).
infra-bot: Alert: cluster:queue-pressure triggered on us-east-1-gpupool-3 at 03:12 UTC (see runbook).
Alex: OK — next step: I'll draft an RFC that includes: routing-hints, cache-affinity metadata, preemptive-flush API, soft-credit admission, observability events, and an incremental rollout plan.
Maria: SGTM. Please include perf goals (p50/p95/p99) and expected unit cost delta.
Prashant: Also include migration strategy for existing queued entries and a togglable feature flag.
Alex: Will do. What should we name it? "adaptive-queue-topology" or "dual-lane-routing"?
Olivia: +1 adaptive-queue-topology.
deploy-bot: RFC template: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/template — Please use the template and add SIG reviewers.
Alex: Thanks — I'll tag eng-runtime + eng-infra and ping y'all when the draft is up.
